full_judgment:
D.C. Bhattacharya, J.— This appeal arises against the judgment and decree dated 25-9-58 by which partition suit No. 25 of 1950 was decreed in preliminary from by the Court of the Additional Subordinate Judge, Dinajpur. After filing the appeal, the learned Advocate for the appellants submitted in application in this Court on 16-5-59. Stating that defendants 3 and 4 of the partition suit died long before the impugned decree and as such the preliminary decree was passed against dead persons, and that as it was a suit for partition, the decree was wholly illegal. The learned Advocate has drawn out attention to the order passed by a Division Bench of the Dacca High Court on the said application should be kept with the record to be considered at the time of the hearing of the appeal. 

 Partition Suit No. 25 of 1950 was originally decreed in a preliminary form on 21-1-52 and against the said preliminary decree an appeal was taken to the Dacca High Court being F.A. No.53 of 1952. It appears from the printed paper books of the said appeal which have been placed before us that defendant No. 4 Mst. Ashia who was respondent No. 12 in the aforesaid appeal died during the pendency of the said appeal and on the basis of the Registrar's Order dated 23-7-54 the heirs of the said deceased respondent were brought on record. The said appeal was ultimately allowed and the decree which as passed was set aside and the case was sent back on remand to the trial court for rehearing. It appears that after remand, the heirs and legal representatives of the deceased defendant No. 4 were not formally brought on record in the suit and the case proceeded against the deceased Mst. Ashia Khatun on record as Defendant No. 4 as if she was still alive. A fresh preliminary decree was passed against Mst. Ashia Khatun on record as Defendant No.4. There are, of course no materials before us as to the death of other defendant viz. Defendant No.3. But the suit being a portion suit and Mst. Asia Khatun being admittedly a co-sharer the decree which has been passed without the heirs of the said deceased defendant being brought on record was illegal and liable to be set aside.
